summary.text: Algebra is a branch of mathematics that deals with abstract systems called algebraic structures and with manipulating expressions within those systems.
It generalizes arithmetic by introducing variables, symbols for unknown or unspecified quantities, which make it possible to state general laws.
Elementary algebra is the form taught in schools, while abstract algebra goes further and studies structures such as groups, rings and fields.

facts.label: Word origin
facts.value: Arabic al-jabr, which originally referred to bonesetting

facts.label: Independent discipline
facts.value: Al-Khwarizmi systematized it in the 9th century, distinct from geometry

facts.label: Symbols arrive
facts.value: A rigorous symbolic formalism developed in the 16th and 17th centuries

facts.label: Scope broadens
facts.value: In the mid-19th century it grew beyond a theory of equations

facts.label: Entered English
facts.value: In the 16th century, from Italian, Spanish and medieval Latin

items.prompt: The equation 2 × 3 = 3 × 2 is true for those numbers. Why does writing a × b = b × a with letters add something?

options.label: It uses a different multiplication operation
It shows 2 and 3 are the only valid numbers
It states a law that holds for any numbers at all
It makes the answer easier to calculate

items.explain: Replacing numbers with variables expresses a general law, here the commutative property of multiplication, that applies to any combination of numbers.

items.prompt: You are told an unknown number makes a statement true, and you want to find which one. What does elementary algebra do?

options.label: Guesses numbers until one happens to fit
Lists every set of objects with an operation on it
Replaces the statement with a bigger, more general structure
Uses a variable and transforms the equation to isolate it

items.explain: Elementary algebra uses variables for unspecified values and transforms equations to isolate them, finding for which values the statements are true.

items.prompt: Three equations share the same unknowns, and you need values that satisfy all of them at once. Which field provides methods for this?

options.label: Linear algebra
Universal algebra
Category theory
Plain arithmetic

items.explain: Linear algebra investigates systems of linear equations and gives methods to find values that solve all the equations at the same time.

items.prompt: What lets abstract algebra reach further than elementary and linear algebra?

options.label: It restricts itself to just the real numbers
It allows non-number objects and non-arithmetic operations
It drops all laws, so anything is allowed
It avoids sets of objects entirely

items.explain: Abstract algebra works with algebraic structures, sets of objects with operations, so it can cover things that are not numbers and operations that are not arithmetic.

items.prompt: Early algebraic methods served particular problems in other fields. What did al-Khwarizmi do in the 9th century?

options.label: Introduced rigorous symbolic notation
Broadened algebra to cover groups and rings
Systematized algebra as its own discipline
Showed algebra was only arithmetic

items.explain: He systematized algebra as an independent mathematical discipline; symbolic notation came in the 16th and 17th centuries and broader structures in the 19th.

items.prompt: Until the 19th century, the word algebra mainly meant which of these?

options.label: The art of manipulating polynomial equations in order to solve them
The study of groups, rings and fields and their axioms
A set with several operations and no equations
A general theory of every possible algebraic structure

items.explain: Its meaning was first restricted to the theory of equations; in the 19th century it broadened to diverse operations and structures and their axioms.
